faq.question: How can I check if my vehicle has a challan?
faq.answer: Go to the official eChallan portal (echallan.parivahan.gov.in, or the NextGen portal at echallan.parivahan.nic.in if your state uses it) and search by vehicle number, driving licence number or challan number. You'll verify with an OTP sent to the registered mobile number. Delhi challans are on the Delhi Traffic Police website.

faq.question: Why does the portal say "no challan found" when I got an SMS?
faq.answer: Usually because your state now uses the NextGen eChallan portal, so search there instead. It can also mean the challan went to court, was issued in Delhi, or that the SMS was fake. Never pay through a link in the message.

faq.question: How many days do I have to pay a traffic challan?
faq.answer: Under the 2026 rules, you have 45 days from issue to pay or contest it on the portal. If you don't contest, it's treated as accepted and must be paid within the next 30 days. Unpaid challans can block licence and registration services.

faq.question: Can I contest a traffic challan online?
faq.answer: Yes, where your state has enabled it. Within 45 days, raise a contest or grievance on the portal with supporting evidence. If it's rejected, you can pay within 30 days or approach the court after depositing 50% of the fine.

faq.question: Is it safe to pay challans through apps like Paytm or car apps?
faq.answer: Some apps show challans correctly, but they may add a convenience fee, and lookalike apps exist. The safest route is the official eChallan portal or the mParivahan app, where you pay only the challan amount.
